## Conference overview

*Preview by Zach Cohen, p. 115. Reproduced in full.*


> Texas Tech stole the headlines in the Big 12 last season, winning the league and grabbing an automatic College Football Playoff berth.

> The Red Raiders did flame out in the postseason, losing 23-0 to Oregon in the quarterfinals.

> However, Joey McGuire’s program officially made its presence felt on the national stage.

> We also saw a tremendous season out of conference runner-up BYU, we witnessed Utah and Houston win double-digit games, and the depth of the league was impressive with nine teams finishing with winning records.

> Heading into the 2026 season, the Red Raiders are once again expected to finish on top.

> However, Texas Tech will have to do it without Brendan Sorsby, who was supposed to take the passing game to another level before a gambling scandal derailed everything.

> The Red Raiders will now need to fight off some much-improved teams without an elite signal-caller.

> Texas Tech is an odds-on favorite to win the Big 12 Conference Championship, but BYU and Utah aren’t too far back on the oddsboard.

> Kansas State, Houston, and Arizona are also shorter than 20-1 at DraftKings Sportsbook, and it’d be foolish to rule out 2024 conference champion Arizona State.

> This simply should be a fascinating year in what has become one of the most interesting leagues in college football. big 12

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 115):**

> Texas Tech stole the headlines in the Big 12 last season, winning the league and grabbing an automatic College Football Playoff berth.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 115*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 16 of 16 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Arizona State Sun Devils** (p. 118) — Well, last year’s 8-5 season felt like a massive disappointment, which is outrageous given this team went 3-9 in 2023.

- **Arizona Wildcats** (p. 116) — Arizona then stumbled to a 4-8 season in 2024, putting Brennan on the hot seat to start 2025.

- **BYU Cougars** (p. 122) — BYU has won double-digit games in four of the last six seasons, and last year’s Cougars squad had a real case for making the College Football Playoff field.

- **Baylor Bears** (p. 121) — Last year, he threw 14 picks and took 19 sacks, making far too many mistakes at the most important position on the field.

- **Cincinnati Bearcats** (p. 124) — Cincinnati finished last season with a 7-6 record, which was somewhat disappointing considering the amount of returning starters (15 who started games the previous year) they had heading into the year.

- **Colorado Buffaloes** (p. 126) — That made for a disaster of a season in 2025, as the Buffs lacked an identity, went 3-9 overall, and finished 1-8 in Big 12 play.

- **Houston Cougars** (p. 128) — Fritz only needed two years to turn Houston into a 10-win team, as last year’s group won nine games and then added a 10th with a victory over LSU in the Texas Bowl.

- **Iowa State Cyclones** (p. 130) — However, Iowa State did pick up a proven winner in Jimmy Rogers, who won a Division I Championship with South Dakota State in 2023 and then did a solid job in his lone season with Washington State last year.
